Determine whether the following reactions represent SPONTANEOUS redox reactions.

Be sure to justify your answer with working, and show half equations with E° values. Finally, show the overall ionic equation with phases and overall E° value for any reactions that occur.

Where a reaction is not predicted you must state this as well as show your working to justify this conclusion.

a. Potassium Fluoride added to Bromine water.

b. Copper added to dilute sulfuric acid.

c. Silver metal added to a solution of zinc nitrate.

d. Magnesium added to a solution of tin (II) sulfate.

e. Sodium Iodide is added to a solution of hydrogen peroxide.

(10 marks)
answerHtml:
Teacher review required. Supplied key is a duplicate blank paper. Newly authored draft answer and suggested allocation require teacher review.

Newly authored draft marking key — teacher review required. The supplied answer file is a duplicate blank paper. Suggested marking allocations follow.

Use the E° values in the class data booklet; small differences between published tables are acceptable.

(a) F₂ + 2e⁻ → 2F⁻, E° ≈ +2.87 V; Br₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Br⁻, E° ≈ +1.09 V. Proposed Br₂ + 2F⁻ → 2Br⁻ + F₂: E°cell ≈ −1.78 V, so no spontaneous reaction.

(b) Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, E° ≈ +0.34 V; 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂, E° = 0.00 V. Proposed Cu + 2H⁺ → Cu²⁺ + H₂: E°cell ≈ −0.34 V; no spontaneous reaction with dilute non-oxidising sulfuric acid.

(c) Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Zn, E° ≈ −0.76 V; Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, E° ≈ +0.80 V. Proposed 2Ag + Zn²⁺ → 2Ag⁺ + Zn: E°cell ≈ −1.56 V; no spontaneous reaction.

(d) Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Mg, E° ≈ −2.37 V; Sn²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Sn, E° ≈ −0.14 V. Mg(s) + Sn²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Sn(s): E°cell ≈ +2.23 V; spontaneous.

(e) In acid: H₂O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → 2H₂O, E° ≈ +1.77 V; I₂ + 2e⁻ → 2I⁻, E° ≈ +0.54 V. H₂O₂(aq) + 2H⁺(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → I₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l), E°cell ≈ +1.23 V; spontaneous. The paper does not specify pH: an alkaline half-equation H₂O₂ + 2e⁻ → 2OH⁻ (E° ≈ +0.88 V) also predicts iodine formation with E°cell ≈ +0.34 V under its standard conditions.

Suggested allocation: 2 marks per part for justified half-equations, E° calculation, and the appropriate conclusion/equation.

(10 marks)
answerHtml:
Teacher review required. Supplied key is a duplicate blank paper. Newly authored draft answer and suggested allocation require teacher review.

Newly authored draft marking key — teacher review required. The supplied answer file is a duplicate blank paper. Suggested marking allocations follow.

Anode (negative): Co(s) → Co²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. Cathode (positive): Sn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Sn(s).

Overall: Co(s) + Sn²⁺(aq) → Co²⁺(aq) + Sn(s). E°cell ≈ −0.14 − (−0.28) = +0.14 V.

Electrons flow through the wire from Co to Sn. The Co electrode loses mass; the Sn electrode gains mass. Co²⁺ enters the cobalt solution; Sn²⁺ moves toward and is deposited on the tin electrode.

In the KNO₃ salt bridge, NO₃⁻ migrates toward the cobalt/anode half-cell and K⁺ toward the tin/cathode half-cell. Electrons do not pass through the salt bridge.

Cell notation: Co(s) | Co²⁺(aq, 1 M) || Sn²⁺(aq, 1 M) | Sn(s).

Suggested allocation: one mark for each of the nine requested features and one for a clear, labelled diagram. Small E° variations following the supplied data booklet are acceptable.
